title: Descartes Colloquium: Herder's Nondualism / The Rise of Women: Making of a Modern Myth
speaker: Vicki A. Spencer (University of Auckland / Senior Descartes Centre Fellow) and Annelien de Dijn (Utrecht University)
location: Johanna Hudig building, room 1.27 (Alex Brenninkmeijer room), entrance Kromme Nieuwegracht 47E
description:
Descartes Centre Colloquium on history & philosophy of science (replaces the UPAC Colloquium this week). Two talks.

Vicki Spencer, "Herder's Nondualism": argues that Herder is better seen as a nondualist than an anti-dualist, offering a positive alternative that blurs the boundaries between mind and body, reason and emotion, and nature and culture, and that this nondualism was already established in his 1772 Treatise on the Origin of Language.

Annelien de Dijn, "The Rise of Women: Making of a Modern Myth": traces the idea that modernisation leads to gender equality from Henry Maine, through Tönnies, Weber and Durkheim, to twentieth-century modernisation theory.

Hybrid; e-mail dc-colloquium@uu.nl for the Teams link.
